ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A horizontal metal ring with a radius of $r=0.2\mathsf{m}$ is fixed. Two metal rods, each with a length of $r$ and a resistance of $R_{0}$, are placed along the diameter of the ring. One end of each rod is in good contact with the ring, and the other end is fixed to a conductive vertical rotating shaft $OO^{\prime}$ passing through the center of the ring. The rods rotate uniformly with an angular velocity of $\omega=600\ rad/s$. A uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of $\mathsf{B}_{1}$ exists in the left half of the ring. The edge of the ring and the brushes in good contact with the rotating shaft are connected to parallel horizontal metal tracks with a distance of $l_{1}$. A capacitor with a capacitance of $C=0.09\ F$ is connected between the tracks. The capacitor can be connected to terminals 1 and 2 via a single-pole double-throw switch S. On the left side of the capacitor is a region with a width of $l_{1}$, a length of $l_{2}$, and a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic induction strength of $B_{2}$. A metal rod $ab$ is placed perpendicularly to the track near the left edge within the magnetic field region. Outside the magnetic field region, there are insulated tracks with a distance of $l_{1}$ smoothly connected to the metal tracks. A "[" shaped metal frame fcde is placed on the horizontal section of the insulated tracks. The length of rod ab and the width of the "[" shaped frame are both $l_{1}$, and their masses are both $m=0.01\ kg$. The lengths of de and $cf$ are both $l_{3}=0.08\ m$. It is known that $l_{1}=0.25\ m$, $l_{2}=0.068\ m$, $B_{1}=B_{2}=1\ T$, and the directions are both vertically upwards. The resistance of the rod ab and the cd side of the "[" shaped frame are both $R=0.1\ \Omega$. Other resistances are negligible. The tracks are smooth, and the rod ab is in good contact with the tracks and remains perpendicular to the tracks during its motion. Initially, the switch S is connected to terminal 1. After the capacitor is fully charged, S is switched from 1 to 2. The capacitor discharges, and the rod ab is ejected out of the magnetic field. The rod ab then sticks to the "[" shaped frame, forming a closed frame abcd. At this point, S is disconnected from 2. It is known that the center of mass of the frame abcd rises by $0.2\ m$ on the inclined track before returning into the magnetic field.

1. Determine the amount of charge $Q$ on the capacitor after it is fully charged, and which plate ($M$ or $N$) is positively charged?
2. Calculate the amount of charge $\Delta Q$ released by the capacitor.
3. Calculate the maximum distance $x$ between side ab and the left boundary of the magnetic field region after the frame abcd enters the magnetic field.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure are a horizontal metal circular ring and a vertical rotating shaft OO′; the left half region of the circular ring is labeled with an upward magnetic field B1, and there is also an arrow at the circular ring indicating the rotation direction; the edge of the circular ring is connected to the upper horizontal rail, and the rotating shaft/brush is connected to the lower horizontal rail. A capacitor is drawn between the two rails, with the upper plate labeled M and the lower plate labeled N, and the single-pole double-throw switch S can connect to 1 or 2. The spacing between the left-side rails is labeled l1, there is an upward B2 magnetic field region in the middle, and its length along the rail direction is labeled l2; metal rod ab is located near this magnetic field region and bridges the two rails; further to the left are insulating rails and a "["-shaped metal frame fcde, whose width is l1, and the horizontal arm length is labeled l3. Reasoning: 1. According to the specified method, regard the rotating double rods and the circular ring on the right side as a DC power source connected between the edge of the circular ring and the rotating shaft. At any moment, only one radial rod is located in the B1 magnetic field in the left semicircle, producing motional electromotive force E = (1/2) B1 ω r^2 = (1/2)×1×600×(0.2)^2 = 12 V. The other rod with equal resistance serves as a circuit branch, so the open-circuit terminal voltage is U = E/2 = 6 V. After the capacitor is fully charged, the charge quantity is Q = C U = 0.09×6 = 0.54 C. Judging from the rotation direction in the figure and the upward B1, the upper rail connected to the edge of the circular ring has higher potential, so the upper plate M of the capacitor is positively charged. 2. After the switch is connected to 2, the capacitor discharges through ab, ab is pushed out of the magnetic field by the Ampere force, and completely inelastically sticks to the equal-mass "["-shaped frame. The total mass after sticking is 2m. After sticking, the closed frame rises to height h=0.2 m and then has zero speed, so the initial speed after sticking satisfies (1/2)(2m)V^2 = (2m)gh, taking g=10 m/s^2, obtain V = sqrt(2gh)=sqrt(2×10×0.2)=2 m/s. Momentum is conserved during the collision process: m v_ab = (2m)V, hence v_ab = 2V = 4 m/s. During the capacitor discharge process, the magnetic-field impulse received by ab is B2 l1 ΔQ = m v_ab, therefore ΔQ = m v_ab/(B2 l1)=0.01×4/(1×0.25)=0.16 C. 3. When the closed frame abcd returns from the left side and enters the B2 region, its speed is still V=2 m/s. The total mass of the closed frame is 2m, and the total resistance is R_tot = R_ab + R_cd = 2R = 0.2 Ω. When only one vertical side cuts the magnetic field boundary, the magnitude of the resistance generated by the induced current is F = B2^2 l1^2 v / R_tot. Thus (2m) dv/dt = -B2^2 l1^2 v/R_tot, and v=dx/dt, so dv/dx = - B2^2 l1^2 /[(2m)R_tot]. Substituting numerical values gives k = B2^2 l1^2 /[(2m)R_tot] = 1^2×0.25^2/(0.02×0.2)=15.625. First segment: ab enters from the left boundary until it leaves the magnetic field, with length l2=0.068 m, and the speed decreases by Δv1 = k l2 = 15.625×0.068 = 1.0625 m/s, hence v1 = 2 - 1.0625 = 0.9375 m/s. Because l3=0.08 m > l2=0.068 m, after ab leaves the magnetic field and before cd reaches the left boundary, the frame is not subject to magnetic resistance, and its speed remains 0.9375 m/s; the length of this uniform-speed segment is l3-l2=0.012 m. At this time, ab is at a distance l3=0.08 m from the left boundary. Second segment: after cd starts entering the magnetic field, it is again subject to the same magnetic resistance. The distance needed to stop is s = v1/k = 0.9375/15.625 = 0.06 m. Therefore, the maximum distance from ab to the left boundary is x = l3 + s = 0.08 + 0.06 = 0.14 m. Final answer: Q=0.54 C, plate M is positively charged; ΔQ=0.16 C; x=0.14 m.
